Siege of Ostend.fact: In 1587, during preparations for the invasion of England by the Spanish Armada, Parma had rejected the idea of a conquest of Ostend by considering it a reckless enterprise after the capture of Sluis.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Ostend was the only possession of the _____ in Flanders and its capture was of strategic importance for the Spanish
Siege of Ostend.fact: Ostend was the only possession of the Dutch Republic in Flanders and its capture was of strategic importance for the Spanish.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The old church and town faced the seas, but in _____ the new town, further inland, was fortified with ramparts, counterscarps, and two broad ditches
Siege of Ostend.fact: The old church and town faced the seas, but in 1583 the new town, further inland, was fortified with ramparts, counterscarps, and two broad ditches.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: A canal called the _____ had begun to form a new harbour on the east side; it was wide, deep, and navigable and served the maritime traffic to the city
Siege of Ostend.fact: A canal called the Geule had begun to form a new harbour on the east side; it was wide, deep, and navigable and served the maritime traffic to the city.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: On the West side of Ostend another canal, the _____, was more of a defensive moat which was barely navigable but could not be easily waded except for four hours at low tide
Siege of Ostend.fact: On the West side of Ostend another canal, the Old Haven, was more of a defensive moat which was barely navigable but could not be easily waded except for four hours at low tide.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: A ditch passed between the old and new towns, which were connected by bridges, and round the new town, parallel to the Geule on one side, and to the old harbour and _____ stream on the other
Siege of Ostend.fact: A ditch passed between the old and new towns, which were connected by bridges, and round the new town, parallel to the Geule on one side, and to the old harbour and Yperlet stream on the other.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In the old town, closer to the mouth of the old harbour, a fort called the _____ had been constructed
Siege of Ostend.fact: In the old town, closer to the mouth of the old harbour, a fort called the Sandhill had been constructed.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: This then linked to the _____, South and West square's; Ostend's most outer defensive works
Siege of Ostend.fact: To the South and West an extensive outwork, the Polder, which had formerly been a field from which the water had been pumped by means of windmills near the point where the Yperlet stream flowed into the old harbour. Flanking the Polder at both points were the South bulwark and the West bulwark, in front of each were two further outworks; the inner stronger Polder, South and West Bulwark's which then linked the Polder, South and West Ravelins.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: They were led by the _____ who was military commander of the Spanish forces in the Low Countries
Siege of Ostend.fact: They were led by the Archduke Albrecht who was military commander of the Spanish forces in the Low Countries.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The defending forces of Ostend were the army of the _____, reorganized by Maurice of Nassau who also played a part in the development of early modern warfare
Siege of Ostend.fact: The defending forces of Ostend were the army of the United Provinces, reorganized by Maurice of Nassau who also played a part in the development of early modern warfare.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The Dutch had large support from their _____ ally England whose pike men and arquebusiers were clad in red cassocks (amongst the earliest English redcoats)
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Dutch had large support from their Protestant ally England whose pike men and arquebusiers were clad in red cassocks (amongst the earliest English redcoats). Other Protestant troops from Scotland, France, and Germany took their side amongst Maurice's army.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Other Protestant troops from _____, France, and Germany took their side amongst Maurice's army
Siege of Ostend.fact: Other Protestant troops from Scotland, France, and Germany took their side amongst Maurice's army.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Sir Francis Vere, the hero of _____, was chosen not as governor, but as general of the army along with ample powers
Siege of Ostend.fact: Sir Francis Vere, the hero of Nieuwpoort, was chosen not as governor, but as general of the army along with ample powers.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The Spanish besiegers soon rose to 20,000, a number which was one of the _____'s preliminary objectives
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish besiegers soon rose to 20,000, a number which was one of the Archduke's preliminary objectives.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: As the _____ cannonaded the city, some soldiers tried to wade the moat but this failed and a number drowned
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish besiegers soon rose to 20,000, a number which was one of the Archduke's preliminary objectives. As the Spanish cannonaded the city, some soldiers tried to wade the moat but this failed and a number drowned.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: These works were constantly interrupted by the rising sea, evolving under fire from the city and in addition the superiority of the Dutch and _____ at sea
Siege of Ostend.fact: These works were constantly interrupted by the rising sea, evolving under fire from the city and in addition the superiority of the Dutch and English at sea. Vere's brother Horace was detached from Maurice's army with eight English companies to reinforce the Ostend garrison.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In addition, the failure of the _____ closing the north side of Ostend enabled it to receive reinforcements and supplies
Siege of Ostend.fact: As the Spanish cannonaded the city, some soldiers tried to wade the moat but this failed and a number drowned. In addition, the failure of the Spanish closing the north side of Ostend enabled it to receive reinforcements and supplies.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere first proceeded to _____ to obtain the approval of Queen Elizabeth, and to raise a body of recruits – these were subsequently raised in East Anglia while some were pressed into service in London
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere first proceeded to England to obtain the approval of Queen Elizabeth, and to raise a body of recruits – these were subsequently raised in East Anglia while some were pressed into service in London.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere's brother _____ was detached from Maurice's army with eight English companies to reinforce the Ostend garrison
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere's brother Horace was detached from Maurice's army with eight English companies to reinforce the Ostend garrison.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Van der _____ met him at the water's edge, and delivered up the keys of Ostend
Siege of Ostend.fact: Van der Noot met him at the water's edge, and delivered up the keys of Ostend.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The garrison then consisted of thirty companies of _____ in two regiments of 2,600 men to which Vere added his eight companies of 100 men each, which brought up the total to 3,500 men
Siege of Ostend.fact: The garrison then consisted of thirty companies of Netherlanders in two regiments of 2,600 men to which Vere added his eight companies of 100 men each, which brought up the total to 3,500 men.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Another 1,500 _____ troops under Edward Cecil arrived on 23 July to build up the garrison
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere's brother Horace was detached from Maurice's army with eight English companies to reinforce the Ostend garrison. Another 1,500 English troops under Edward Cecil arrived on 23 July to build up the garrison.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Amongst the killed was _____, son of a former secretary of state to Philip II
Siege of Ostend.fact: Amongst the killed was Don Diego Idiaquez, son of a former secretary of state to Philip II.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: On 4 August the _____ kept up a tremendous fire on the town from all their batteries, and Sir Francis Vere was severely wounded in the head
Siege of Ostend.fact: On 4 August the Spaniards kept up a tremendous fire on the town from all their batteries, and Sir Francis Vere was severely wounded in the head.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere went to _____ to be treated for his wound, and in a few weeks he was convalescent
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere went to Middelburg to be treated for his wound, and in a few weeks he was convalescent.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In September he returned to Ostend along with more recruits from _____, England, and Scotland
Siege of Ostend.fact: In September he returned to Ostend along with more recruits from Holland, England, and Scotland.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Meanwhile, the fire from the besiegers continued and the soldiers of the garrison dug underground quarters in the marketplace near the "_____" bastion, for protection against the hail of shot
Siege of Ostend.fact: Meanwhile, the fire from the besiegers continued and the soldiers of the garrison dug underground quarters in the marketplace near the "Pekel" bastion, for protection against the hail of shot.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The States General at this time demanded that _____ should march to relieve the city; to take on the besiegers
Siege of Ostend.fact: The States General at this time demanded that Maurice should march to relieve the city; to take on the besiegers. Vere was himself frustrated at both the lack of Dutch response from the States General and from Maurice; particularly when a few veteran companies including Edward Cecil's, were taken out of Ostend to join Maurice's forces back in the field.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Maurice however knowing the futility in making a direct attack, chose to campaign in the surrounding areas in an attempt to block the _____ supplies and divert the attention of the besiegers
Siege of Ostend.fact: Maurice however knowing the futility in making a direct attack, chose to campaign in the surrounding areas in an attempt to block the Spanish supplies and divert the attention of the besiegers. He laid siege to and retook Rheinberg and then continued to Spanish-held Meurs in August which was also captured.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: He laid siege to and retook _____ and then continued to Spanish-held Meurs in August which was also captured
Siege of Ostend.fact: He laid siege to and retook Rheinberg and then continued to Spanish-held Meurs in August which was also captured.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Maurice hoped to take 's-_____ but plans for the siege were cancelled and so withdrew to winter quarters
Siege of Ostend.fact: Maurice hoped to take 's-Hertogenbosch but plans for the siege were cancelled and so withdrew to winter quarters.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: He began to convey intelligence to the besiegers under an agreement with _____
Siege of Ostend.fact: He began to convey intelligence to the besiegers under an agreement with Albert.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: A boat was sunk in the mud, on the banks of the Old haven, near the South square; _____ was to deposit letters there from which a Spanish soldier then took them during the night
Siege of Ostend.fact: A boat was sunk in the mud, on the banks of the Old haven, near the South square; Conisby was to deposit letters there from which a Spanish soldier then took them during the night. Conisby however grew bolder, and tried to bribe a sergeant to blow up the powder magazine.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The sergeant revealed the plot and _____ confessed to everything, and was sentenced to be publicly executed but in an act of clemency was whipped out of the town
Siege of Ostend.fact: A boat was sunk in the mud, on the banks of the Old haven, near the South square; Conisby was to deposit letters there from which a Spanish soldier then took them during the night. Conisby however grew bolder, and tried to bribe a sergeant to blow up the powder magazine.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: On 4 _____ a breach was made in between the Porcespic and the Helmund and the Archduke was prepared to storm
Siege of Ostend.fact: On 4 December a breach was made in between the Porcespic and the Helmund and the Archduke was prepared to storm.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere made sure it was heavily guarded and placed _____'s company there but was awoken by the alarm and rushed to the ramparts to discover the Spanish were assaulting the breach
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere made sure it was heavily guarded and placed Sir John Ogle's company there but was awoken by the alarm and rushed to the ramparts to discover the Spanish were assaulting the breach.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: A force of 3 – 4,000 _____ attempted to storm the position; the phalanx of Spanish pikemen managed to gain the breach but were forced out by a counterattack
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere made sure it was heavily guarded and placed Sir John Ogle's company there but was awoken by the alarm and rushed to the ramparts to discover the Spanish were assaulting the breach. A force of 3 – 4,000 Spanish attempted to storm the position; the phalanx of Spanish pikemen managed to gain the breach but were forced out by a counterattack.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The assault never made it past the breach as the _____ found the rubble almost impossible to fight on and suffered heavy casualties
Siege of Ostend.fact: A force of 3 – 4,000 Spanish attempted to storm the position; the phalanx of Spanish pikemen managed to gain the breach but were forced out by a counterattack. The Spanish then launched further attacks but were repelled again.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In the end the attack was a disaster and after half an hour the _____ had lost over 500 men, nearly a quarter of the attacking force
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish then launched further attacks but were repelled again. The assault never made it past the breach as the Spanish found the rubble almost impossible to fight on and suffered heavy casualties.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Furthermore, the outer works such as the _____ had to be temporarily abandoned because of storms and exposed icy conditions
Siege of Ostend.fact: Furthermore, the outer works such as the Polder had to be temporarily abandoned because of storms and exposed icy conditions.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: On 23 _____, Vere learned from a deserter that the Spanish were in preparation for a large impending assault on the city; he realized he had no hope except to hold for time
Siege of Ostend.fact: On 23 December, Vere learned from a deserter that the Spanish were in preparation for a large impending assault on the city; he realized he had no hope except to hold for time.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: He therefore proposed a parley to the _____ for negotiations; but this was a ploy hoping to gain time to await the arrival of the reinforcements
Siege of Ostend.fact: He therefore proposed a parley to the Spaniards for negotiations; but this was a ploy hoping to gain time to await the arrival of the reinforcements.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere then construed as much time as possible frustrating _____ 'negotiations'; he ordered his men to beat to quarters even though there was no attack
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish accepted and Vere sent two of his captains, John Ogle and Charles Fairfax, as hostages to the Spanish camp, while the Spanish sent in return Mateo Antonio, quartermaster general of the Spanish army, and Matteo Serrano, Governor of Sluis, to negotiate terms of possible surrender. Vere then construed as much time as possible frustrating Spanish 'negotiations'; he ordered his men to beat to quarters even though there was no attack.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere then expressed anger at _____ and Antonio as to why the Spanish had intended to attack and then refused to speak with them
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish accepted and Vere sent two of his captains, John Ogle and Charles Fairfax, as hostages to the Spanish camp, while the Spanish sent in return Mateo Antonio, quartermaster general of the Spanish army, and Matteo Serrano, Governor of Sluis, to negotiate terms of possible surrender. Vere then expressed anger at Serrano and Antonio as to why the Spanish had intended to attack and then refused to speak with them.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere then ordered them to stay put because of the dark and high tide, and flagons of _____ ale were given as compensation
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere then ordered them to stay put because of the dark and high tide, and flagons of English ale were given as compensation.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The next day they arrived back at _____'s headquarters; but he immediately sent them back
Siege of Ostend.fact: The next day they arrived back at Albert's headquarters; but he immediately sent them back.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Negotiations had been held off for twenty-four hours and _____ stated that the incident was a total misunderstanding and apologized
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere then ordered them to stay put because of the dark and high tide, and flagons of English ale were given as compensation. Negotiations had been held off for twenty-four hours and Vere stated that the incident was a total misunderstanding and apologized.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere told _____ and Antonio that the archduke must withdraw from Ostend or surrender his forces; the reply was the Archduke was to see the surrender of the town
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere told Serrano and Antonio that the archduke must withdraw from Ostend or surrender his forces; the reply was the Archduke was to see the surrender of the town.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere then broke off the discussions again and both were invited to a banquet as it was _____ which they accepted with more time wasted
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere then broke off the discussions again and both were invited to a banquet as it was Christmas Eve which they accepted with more time wasted.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Rumours began to circulate outside that Ostend had fallen and the _____ and Isabella had dressed in their best to await the surrender
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere told Serrano and Antonio that the archduke must withdraw from Ostend or surrender his forces; the reply was the Archduke was to see the surrender of the town. Rumours began to circulate outside that Ostend had fallen and the Archduke and Isabella had dressed in their best to await the surrender.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In the town however both _____ and Antonio were about to resume talks but during the night three ships arrived with 600 Zeelanders as reinforcements
Siege of Ostend.fact: In the town however both Serano and Antonio were about to resume talks but during the night three ships arrived with 600 Zeelanders as reinforcements.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The Spanish, in particular the archduke, were outraged; reluctantly they released Ogle and _____ once Serrano and Antonio had returned
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish, in particular the archduke, were outraged; reluctantly they released Ogle and Fairfax once Serrano and Antonio had returned.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Horace Vere and _____, with 12 companies armed with pikes and muskets, were stationed in the "Sand-hill"
Siege of Ostend.fact: Horace Vere and Charles Fairfax, with 12 companies armed with pikes and muskets, were stationed in the "Sand-hill".

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere took his stand with six of his veteran _____ and Scots companies close by
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere took his stand with six of his veteran English and Scots companies close by. Two more companies, one English and one Dutch, occupied the Schottenburgh redoubt and from there to the destroyed church were 300 Zeelanders who had arrived on the 26th.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Two more companies, one _____ and one Dutch, occupied the Schottenburgh redoubt and from there to the destroyed church were 300 Zeelanders who had arrived on the 26th
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere took his stand with six of his veteran English and Scots companies close by. Two more companies, one English and one Dutch, occupied the Schottenburgh redoubt and from there to the destroyed church were 300 Zeelanders who had arrived on the 26th.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Ten Dutch companies occupied positions from the church, "_____", North ravelin, and "Flamenburgh", while four large guns protected the harbour and the old town
Siege of Ostend.fact: Ten Dutch companies occupied positions from the church, "Moses Table", North ravelin, and "Flamenburgh", while four large guns protected the harbour and the old town.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The two most important works, flanking the breach, the "_____" and the "Helmund", held ten Dutch and English companies along with nine guns loaded with grape shot
Siege of Ostend.fact: The two most important works, flanking the breach, the "Porcespic" and the "Helmund", held ten Dutch and English companies along with nine guns loaded with grape shot.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: In the "_____" two demi-culverins were placed to sweep the old haven
Siege of Ostend.fact: In the "West Bulwark" two demi-culverins were placed to sweep the old haven.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: By the evening the _____ army had marshalled for a huge assault and were seen bringing down scaling ladders and ammunition
Siege of Ostend.fact: By the evening the Spanish army had marshalled for a huge assault and were seen bringing down scaling ladders and ammunition. Count Farnese, with 2,000 Spanish and Italian troops, were ordered to attack the "Sandhill" and the curtain of the old town wall.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Count Farnese, with 2,000 _____ and Italian troops, were ordered to attack the "Sandhill" and the curtain of the old town wall
Siege of Ostend.fact: By the evening the Spanish army had marshalled for a huge assault and were seen bringing down scaling ladders and ammunition. Count Farnese, with 2,000 Spanish and Italian troops, were ordered to attack the "Sandhill" and the curtain of the old town wall.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The governor of _____, with 2,000 Spaniards, was to assault "Helmund" and the Porcespic; a force of 500 men was to scale the west ravelin, while a similar number attacked the "South Square"
Siege of Ostend.fact: The governor of Dixmunde, with 2,000 Spaniards, was to assault "Helmund" and the Porcespic; a force of 500 men was to scale the west ravelin, while a similar number attacked the "South Square".

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Along the curtain of the old town, the _____ rushed into the breach but as they climbed up they were met by ordnance fire from the bulwarks
Siege of Ostend.fact: The governor of Dixmunde, with 2,000 Spaniards, was to assault "Helmund" and the Porcespic; a force of 500 men was to scale the west ravelin, while a similar number attacked the "South Square".

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: On the east side _____ was to deliver an assault, specially attacking the east ravelin and the defences of the new haven; in all the assault totalled some 10,000 men
Siege of Ostend.fact: On the east side Count Bucquoy was to deliver an assault, specially attacking the east ravelin and the defences of the new haven; in all the assault totalled some 10,000 men.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The Archduke fired a gun as a signal to _____, and the besiegers rushed to the assault from all points just as the darkness of night set in
Siege of Ostend.fact: On the east side Count Bucquoy was to deliver an assault, specially attacking the east ravelin and the defences of the new haven; in all the assault totalled some 10,000 men. The Archduke fired a gun as a signal to Bucquoy, and the besiegers rushed to the assault from all points just as the darkness of night set in.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere's engineers immediately discovered _____ wading across with his 2,000 Italians, and drawing them up in battalions on the Ostend side
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere's engineers immediately discovered Count Farnese wading across with his 2,000 Italians, and drawing them up in battalions on the Ostend side.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere then went to the top of the "_____" and issued orders to have everything in readiness, but not to fire until he gave the signal, and then to open with both ordnance and small shot
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere then went to the top of the "Sandhill" and issued orders to have everything in readiness, but not to fire until he gave the signal, and then to open with both ordnance and small shot. As the Spanish approached ever closer Vere at once ordered a heavy fire on to the Spanish battalions heading towards the foot of the "Sandhill".

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: As the _____ approached ever closer Vere at once ordered a heavy fire on to the Spanish battalions heading towards the foot of the "Sandhill"
Siege of Ostend.fact: As the Spanish approached ever closer Vere at once ordered a heavy fire on to the Spanish battalions heading towards the foot of the "Sandhill". The Spanish no sooner climbed to the crest of the "Sandhill" and the "Schottenburgh" but were repelled three times with heavy losses after rallying to the charge, while the struggle on the breach continued during the space of an hour.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Similar assaults were made on the Western ravelin, and on the "_____", while on the east side three strong battalions of the Spanish were formed on the margin of the "Geule"
Siege of Ostend.fact: Similar assaults were made on the Western ravelin, and on the "South Square", while on the east side three strong battalions of the Spanish were formed on the margin of the "Geule".

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: They then attacked the "_____-moon" outwork which was taken after heavy fighting
Siege of Ostend.fact: They then attacked the "Spanish Half-moon" outwork which was taken after heavy fighting.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Vere ordered its recovery and heavy fire was opened from the bulwarks and then an _____ company drove them out with a loss of 300 men, mostly captured
Siege of Ostend.fact: Vere ordered its recovery and heavy fire was opened from the bulwarks and then an English company drove them out with a loss of 300 men, mostly captured.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: By midnight the _____ were repulsed at all points having suffered heavily in the assault and were milling about in the ford in confusion
Siege of Ostend.fact: Similar assaults were made on the Western ravelin, and on the "South Square", while on the east side three strong battalions of the Spanish were formed on the margin of the "Geule". They then attacked the "Spanish Half-moon" outwork which was taken after heavy fighting.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: The English were first into the fray; _____ pistols, priest's cassocks, swords, gold chains, pendants, and enamelled shields were all taken from the dead and dying
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish retreated in complete disorder throwing away everything they had. The English were first into the fray; Spanish pistols, priest's cassocks, swords, gold chains, pendants, and enamelled shields were all taken from the dead and dying.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: There were heaps of _____ and Italian dead under the "Sandhill" and along the wall of the old town, amidst broken siege equipment
Siege of Ostend.fact: The Spanish retreated in complete disorder throwing away everything they had. The English were first into the fray; Spanish pistols, priest's cassocks, swords, gold chains, pendants, and enamelled shields were all taken from the dead and dying.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Coronel Don Alvarez Suarez (_____ of the Order of Santiago) lost his life as well as Coronel Simon Antonio
Siege of Ostend.fact: Coronel Don Alvarez Suarez (Knight of the Order of Santiago) lost his life as well as Coronel Simon Antonio.

Siege of Ostend.subject: Women & Society
Siege of Ostend.question: Among the deads was furthermore the hostage during the parley (_____ mayor Ottanes?) and also the Lieutenant Governor of Antwerp
Siege of Ostend.fact: Among the deads was furthermore the hostage during the parley (Sargento mayor Ottanes?) and also the Lieutenant Governor of Antwerp.
